html:
The Syr Darya is a river of Central Asia, about 2,200 km long. It rises in the Tian Shan mountains, flows west through the Fergana Valley, then northwest across the deserts of Kazakhstan to the Aral Sea. The Greeks called it the Jaxartes.

For much of history it marked the edge between the farmed oasis lands to the south and the steppe of the nomads to the north. It was the northeastern frontier of the Persian Empire. Alexander the Great founded Alexandria Eschate, "the furthest", on its banks in 329 BCE, where Khujand stands today.

Trading towns grew along its middle course. At Otrar, in 1218, the killing of a caravan sent by Genghis Khan brought on the Mongol invasion of Khwarazm. Further down, Turkestan holds the Mausoleum of Ahmed Yasawi.

In the Soviet era its water was taken for cotton through canals such as the Great Fergana Canal, and little reached the sea, which began to shrink. A dam built in 2005 now holds its flow in the northern part of the sea, and the fishery has come back. The Baikonur Cosmodrome lies on its banks in Kazakhstan.
